author: FractalDataWorks
name: Reference API host (authentication + configuration gateway)
description: A runnable API host wired the way the reference stack expects: configurationSchema.json declaring the ServerConfiguration and PlatformConfiguration connections, Connection/SecretManager/ConfigurationGateway registered ahead of the three-phase PlatformServices lifecycle, and token-issuing authentication via FdwReferenceAuth.Endpoints.

SecretManager.description: Which secret manager option this host registers. A SqlAuth PlatformConfiguration connection names it in SecretManagerName to resolve its password. Secret managers are configured in PlatformConfiguration itself, so the PlatformConfiguration password cannot come from a manager that is read out of it — see the README.

choices.description: Read secrets from sec.Secret in ConfigurationDb.

DbServer.description: ConfigurationDb host name or IP, written into configurationSchema.json. Server-backed types only; ignored for Sqlite and FileSystem.

DbName.description: The ConfigurationDb catalogue this host reads its configuration from. Server-backed types only; ignored for Sqlite and FileSystem.

DbPort.description: SQL Server port. Server-backed types only; ignored for Sqlite and FileSystem.

DbUser.description: SQL login this host connects as. Its password is never written here — see SecretKeyName. Server-backed types only; ignored for Sqlite and FileSystem.

SecretKeyName.description: Logical name of the PlatformConfiguration password, resolved through the named secret manager. SqlAuth only.

AuthenticationType.description: How this host authenticates to ConfigurationDb. Only SqlAuth has a password, and so only SqlAuth needs a secret manager for the connection. Server-backed types only; ignored for Sqlite and FileSystem.

choices.description: SQL login and password. Needs a secret manager to supply the password.
Azure managed identity. No password, no secret manager for the connection.
The developer's az login. No password. Local use only.

ConnectionType.description: Where this host reads its configuration from. The server-backed types ask for a server, database and credentials; the file-backed types ask only for a path.

choices.description: SQL Server. Asks for server, database, port, login and how the password is supplied.
PostgreSQL. Same details as SQL Server.
A SQLite file. Asks only for the file path.
Configuration held as files on disk. Asks only for the directory path.

ConfigPath.description: File-backed types only: the SQLite file (DataSource) or the configuration directory (Root) for PlatformConfiguration. Ignored for MsSql and PostgreSql.

ServerConfigRoot.description: Root directory of the ServerConfiguration FileSystem connection: the host's own boot-time rows (logging, authentication, the host record). Read before PlatformConfiguration is reachable, which is why it is files and not a database.
